topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer frames the session by reviewing prior histopathology practicals and setting out the core learning outcomes on cellular transformation, oncogenes, and genetic instability.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes through tumor virology and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the historical study of transforming viruses, the realization that viral oncogenes derive from cellular proto-oncogenes, and the experimental laboratory assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional properties and mutation mechanics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer-associated genes, illustrate their regulatory roles in cell cycle checkpoints, and examine the genetic consequences of dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing the specific failures in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic segregation that generate genome-wide abnormalities.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the stepwise accumulation of mutations in tumor development and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this progression across distinct cancer predisposition syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by confirming the coverage of learning objectives, recommending follow-up reading, and previewing the next lecture.
